accuracy.evidence: Word lists and terms match the English national curriculum Year 3 vocabulary, grammar and punctuation appendix: express time, place and cause using conjunctions (when, before, after, while, so, because), adverbs (then, next, soon, therefore) and prepositions (before, after, during, in, because of); terms conjunction, clause, subordinate clause, adverb, preposition. Fronted adverbial clauses take a comma (Year 4 appendix). Every lab answer was checked: 'because' introduces the cause, 'so' the result, 'while' simultaneity, and the comma sits after 'rang'.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS2 slips: reversing cause and result by swapping because/so (join rounds 1-2 and the cause-builder), flipping order with before/after (round 3, challenge 'Ali packed his bag'), 'then, then, then' narration (story step), muddling 'in' as time vs place (sort feedback), and misplacing the comma inside a fronted clause (comma step and challenge).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanics are this topic's own: dropping conjunctions into a gap between two clauses with meaning-specific feedback for each wrong word, putting time adverbs on story sentences, sorting prepositional phrases into when/where/why, ordering cause and result around because/so, and moving a subordinate clause to the front then tapping the comma gap. The shingle gate passed against every flag_*.js lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each wrong drop explains what the sentence would then mean ('That says going inside made it rain!'), so the learner discovers that the joining word carries the meaning; the cause-builder makes them notice that the cause sits after 'because' but before 'so'; the comma step shows the comma marks the end of the fronted clause. The step text confirms after each task.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'so' for 'We went inside ___ it was raining' (the common reversal), 'when' for 'because of the rain' (a preposition phrase that looks like a time phrase), and 'after so' for where the cause goes (true for 'because', false for 'so'); each is disproved by the lab feedback.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve tagged messages that name the slip: reversed cause with 'so' and with 'because', 'then' giving only order, 'Before that' flipping order, 'after' meaning he had already left, 'Because' used as a time word, leaving as a non-reason, time and why phrases picked for where, comma after 'we', comma after 'When', and 'while' for a cause.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation measures FK grade 1.4 (family limit 5.0) with short example sentences; adult text is FK 8.2 (limit 10). Canvas prompts are one line; button labels are the words themselves plus short 'Comma after rang' style labels.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and 12% duplicate gate. Kid paragraphs cover time words, cause words, the because/so reversal, avoiding 'then', and phrases; adult paragraphs cover curriculum placement and terms, clause structure, the three common slips and the fronted comma. Each lab step has a separate job.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android screenshots of all six steps in light and dark: the clause pieces and conjunction tiles wrap to centred rows, the four story rows fit after shortening the last sentence (it first wrapped into the tile row), the three when/where/why bins fit side by side, and the cause and comma steps fit on one or two rows. Every action also has a full-width button below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task completes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes, and there are no console errors. Every drag has a button route (conjunction buttons, adverb buttons naming the sentence, when/where/why buttons, cause/result buttons, a move button and 'Comma after …' buttons), and the canvas aria-label states the result of each move.

sources: Department for Education (2013), English programmes of study: key stages 1 and 2, Appendix 2 Vocabulary, grammar and punctuation, Year 3 (express time, place and cause using conjunctions, adverbs and prepositions) and Year 4 (fronted adverbials with a comma)
Department for Education (2013), English Appendix 2 terminology for pupils: conjunction, clause, subordinate clause, adverb, preposition
Standards and Testing Agency, KS2 English grammar, punctuation and spelling test framework: subordinating conjunctions and commas after fronted adverbials
